timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only CLI stream reviewed through manifest accounting; semantic actions are projected in raw agent timelines.
Serial single-agent trajectory reviewed for implementation edits, tests, cleanup, and final response.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the xlrd project requirements: .xls reading, documented API surface, CLI, packaging, examples, and tests; used the shared prompt and upstream-compatible xlrd target.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent copied/ported upstream xlrd, made direct implementation fixes, and launched a broad read-only workflow audit with one auditor per spec slice and verifier children for reported gaps.
parallel.implementation: Implemented top-level exports, USE_MMAP compatibility, Book attributes, packaging, and documentation/test-related fixes while preserving the upstream test baseline; audit children reported many conformance observations.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The workspace artifact copied successfully and official tests later passed, but the agent process did not close normally and the final response file is empty.
parallel.verification: Parallel children repeatedly ran targeted probes and baseline pytest checks; official evaluation completed afterward with 84 of 84 passing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official correctness failure remains, but the workflow fan-out consumed the closure budget, leaving process_ok false, timed_out true, and no final answer text.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same xlrd requirements and API/CLI/package/test obligations from the prompt without delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used one agent to download/copy upstream xlrd, inspect gaps, apply fixes, add tests/examples, and run final verification.
serial.implementation: Fixed missing top-level exports and USE_MMAP, added documented Book aliases, adjusted MANIFEST, created examples and API-surface tests, and kept the compatible hex dump behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Produced a coherent workspace with requirements, examples, tests, scripts, docs, and a nonempty final response summarizing the completed work.
serial.verification: Ran upstream tests, expanded API-surface tests, CLI checks, sample sweeps, compileall, setup checks, and an isolated install; final local suite reported 117 passing tests and official evaluation reported 84 of 84.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official correctness failure remains; final text notes that the submit tool was unavailable but the later official status record completed successfully.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full xlrd compatibility task and even launched an exhaustive spec-conformance audit workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same implementation, API, CLI, packaging, examples, and test requirements from the prompt.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-coverage difference affected official outcome; the difference is that parallel spent additional budget on a very broad delegated audit.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent kept implementation ownership but delegated a 12-slice audit and verifier phase to many child agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all investigation, implementation, testing, and cleanup in one non-delegated trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a heavy parallel audit decomposition; serial used sequential ownership and avoided child coordination overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs were read-only audit prompts with concrete spec slices and verifier schemas, so the child interface was reporting findings rather than writing code.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept task knowledge local, so there were no child handoffs or cross-agent contracts to maintain.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No context-transfer bug is retained; the relevant contrast is parallel report fan-out versus serial local context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel copied/ported xlrd and applied direct fixes informed partly by audit results; official artifact validation listed the expected package, scripts, docs, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial copied upstream xlrd, fixed the API surface, CLI USE_MMAP, Book attributes, manifest, examples, and tests, then reported those fixes explicitly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both reached a passing implementation; serial made the path clearer and finished with a documented summary, while parallel had extra audit overhead.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow generated many child starts and some results, but the parent process timed out before normal final response closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reached normal end_turn and wrote a complete final response after verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result lifecycle had residual workflow/closure pressure; serial retrieved its own results and closed normally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child work was read-only auditing, while the parent wrote the implementation; artifact validation found a coherent workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single workspace writer and cleaned temporary/cache artifacts before final verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state collision explains the pair; parallel shared-state risk did not materialize into a write conflict.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran many child probes and official evaluation passed 84 of 84; however the process did not finish with a normal final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran 117 local tests plus broader checks and official evaluation passed 84 of 84.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Official acceptance is equal, but serial had cleaner self-contained verification and closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed essentially the whole 2400-second cell budget with 57 child logs and exited with return code 143; final.txt has zero lines.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial exited return code 0 in 1957.84 seconds with about 440 seconds remaining and a nonempty final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main task-solving difference is closure: both artifacts pass, but parallel exhausted budget through fan-out while serial completed cleanly.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial pass 84 of 84 tests. The concrete difference is process and delivery, not scored correctness: parallel used a broad child-agent audit that consumed the time budget and left an empty final response, while serial solved the task in one trajectory and exited normally with a final summary.
parallel_contributors: Broad audit/verifier workflow produced 57 workflow child logs and consumed the closure budget before a final response.
serial_contributors: Single-agent control avoided delegation overhead and completed with return code 0, remaining budget, and a written final summary.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial added an examples/read_excel.py demo, requirements, and 33 additional API-surface tests; both artifacts still passed the same official 84-test evaluation.

candidates.reason: Parallel had a main implementation owner and later task reminders for export, setup, examples, and audit fixes; missing implementation ownership is not the boundary.
The work was not split into independently owned component implementations needing reconciliation; the parent handled integration of fixes.
The parent assembled the workspace artifact and official artifact validation succeeded; the adverse episode is timeout after broad audit fan-out, not an unowned deliverable.
The parent owned the end-to-end pipeline from implementation to tests and artifact delivery, even though the workflow audit consumed the closure budget.
No mandatory serial preflight blocked implementation; the workflow audit ran after substantial implementation work and alongside parent activity.
The child agents were parallel auditors/verifiers, not a separated investigation phase that deferred all implementation until too late.
The evidence points to collective breadth exhausting the whole budget rather than an indispensable implementation path starved while auxiliary work received capacity.

The parent launched an exhaustive workflow with many audit slices and a second verifier phase, producing dozens of child logs. That breadth consumed the finite run budget: the parallel process returned 143 at 2399.544 seconds against the 2400-second budget and left no final response, even though the artifact later passed official tests. The serial control solved and verified the same project without delegation and exited normally with a final summary and remaining budget.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel run exhausted its closure budget and lost normal delivery closure: process_ok was false, timed_out was true, and final.txt was empty despite a passing artifact.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did not simply wait blindly; it launched and polled a very broad workflow. The correction would be limiting or staging the fan-out, not merely adding progress inspection.

candidates.reason: No single child assignment is the dominant overbroad task; the episode is the aggregate slice and verifier fan-out across many children.
The audit-child briefs included concrete spec slices, environment context, read-only scope, and empirical verification requirements; no omitted known requirement made returned work unusable.
Children were not separately implementing interdependent components with absent file, namespace, or API contracts; they produced audit findings.
There is no evidence a known finding was lost through summary or transfer and then repeated by the receiver.
Several child reports were large, but the retained adverse consequence is budget exhaustion from broad fan-out, not a specific available handoff that the parent could not reduce.
No child result was consumed after becoming superseded by a newer workspace state in a way that caused rework or invalid verification.
The audit produced disagreements such as hex-dump interpretation, but there is no parent decision point with incompatible handoffs left unadjudicated as the concrete adverse event.
The parallel parent did not make a final whole-task completion claim before closure; official status passed later and evaluator records cannot establish this context label.
Repeated verifier starts were part of the broad workflow pipeline, not a replacement retry that lacked inherited state and repeated the same failed work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Interrupted child symptoms belong to the same fan-out timeout chain; the directly evidenced corrective boundary is reducing breadth or verifier fan-out, not one premature stop.
A passing workspace artifact was already present; no complete but unpromoted deliverable candidate was left outside the final tree. The missing final response is downstream closure loss.
No specific child result or implementation change is shown as merged after integrated verification without a closing check.
The delegated work was read-only audit/verification, not a completed implementation artifact that the parent failed to retrieve or adopt.
Any absent or late verifier aggregation is downstream of the same collective fan-out budget exhaustion episode and is not a separate result-lifecycle failure.
No required child implementation failure is shown to have been abandoned without takeover; the parent proceeded with direct implementation and official tests passed.
The parent inspected audit status and applied fixes; there is no concrete completed child result that was visible, ignored, and contradicted by subsequent action.
The parent repeatedly inspected workflow progress and counts; the adverse event was too much fan-out for the budget rather than passive waiting without inspection.
The child workflow was explicitly read-only and the parent wrote the implementation; no competing cross-file implementation ownership required reconciliation.
There is no evidence that live agents edited the same source file and one had to reconcile another's concurrent change.
No child-owned library or configuration source was replaced by another live actor.
No submitted entry point or executable deliverable was overwritten while another agent owned or used it.
No broad cleanup or promotion replaced another actor's final-tree output; artifact validation saw a coherent workspace.
Although many agents shared the workspace for reading, the workflow brief forbade child writes and no unstable write provenance issue is shown.
There is no evidence a generated child artifact, cache, temp path, or process was consumed as stable input by another actor and contaminated verification.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Critical-Path Starvation, Oversized Child Task, Early Child Termination, Missing Verifier Return, No Failure Takeover, Blind Timeout Wait, and Late Finalization were considered as timeout-chain symptoms and rejected because they do not have a distinct episode, consequence, and corrective action.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the fan-out budget episode clears the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The broad workflow timeout was treated as one chain, so downstream child interruption, missing aggregate return, and empty final-response symptoms were not split into additional labels.
